## Format

> Source: the live guide for authors (https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/computers-in-human-behavior-artificial-humans/publish/guide-for-authors; identical text at https://www.elsevier.com/journals/computers-in-human-behavior-artificial-humans/2949-8821/guide-for-authors), read 2026-11-23, with the archived guide (copy dated 2024-06-03) as the older dated source. Both contain publisher template text for peer review, structure, abstract, keywords and references; neither has an article-type list or a word limit. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | The aims text (journal home copy, 2025-08-25) says the journal welcomes "original research, reviews, or other contributions". OpenAlex type counts, 2023-01-01 to 2026-11-23: 350 articles, 17 errata, 10 paratext, 9 reviews, 1 editorial (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit** | Blank. No readable page states a word or page limit for this journal; the live guide (2026-11-23) states none either, its only length figure being the 250-word abstract |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. No limit found, so nothing to negotiate |
| **Abstract limit** | 250 words: the live guide (read 2026-11-23) requires a concise, factual, stand-alone abstract that "does not exceed 250 words", 1 to 7 keywords in English, and encourages a graphical abstract. Highlights, 3 to 5 bullets of at most 85 characters each, are optional. The 2024 archived guide gave no abstract word count and at most 6 keywords (older dated reading) |
| **Reference limit** | No cap found. Live guide (2026-11-23): in-text citations follow APA 7th edition, with an alphabetical reference list; the 2024 archived guide had numbered references in square brackets in order of appearance (older dated reading) |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed: the live guide (2026-11-23) encourages supplementary material such as applications, images and sound clips, to be submitted with the manuscript and cited in the text; the archived guide also says the journal "encourages and enables" data sharing |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Live guide (2026-11-23): tables as editable text, numbered consecutively, with captions; photographs at a minimum of 300 dpi and bitmapped line drawings at a minimum of 1000 dpi |
| **Style / submission format** | Live guide (read 2026-11-23): .doc/.docx or .tex source files (not PDF); Word files in a single-column layout; separate title page and anonymized manuscript; American or British English but not a mixture; 1 to 7 keywords; sections numbered 1, 1.1, 1.1.1; footnotes used sparingly; APA 7th citations. Older dated reading (archived guide, 2024-06-03): at most 6 keywords in American spelling, numbered references; Crossref Similarity Check may be run on submissions |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes, a scope condition is stated by the journal itself: the journal examines artificial agents (social robots, algorithm-based agents, AI), human interactions with them, interactions through technological implants, and acceptance of direct human-computer interfaces, from a psychological perspective (aims text, journal home copy dated 2025-08-25, https://web.archive.org/web/20250825002333/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/computers-in-human-behavior-artificial-humans). Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** The aims text says the journal focuses on psychological or societal aspects of these interactions, not on purely technical issues, and will consider contributions from psychology, neuroscience, neurobiology, anthropology, human-machine interaction, philosophy, sociology or Internet studies, using models including social robots, algorithms, cyborgs, AI or drones.
- **Position within a family**: the aims text says the journal is more specialised than Computers in Human Behavior and Computers in Human Behavior Reports and keeps the same demands of scientific excellence (same page).
- **Ethics statements required by the guide**: for human-subject work, a statement that procedures complied with laws and institutional guidelines and were approved by the appropriate committee, including the date and reference number, plus a statement that informed consent was obtained (archived guide, 2024-06-03).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: no source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions, and no desk-rejection data exists for this journal (SciRev and LetPub pages not found).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts: records of this source dated 2023-01-01 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex works API, 387 records; 352 with an abstract). Shares use the 352 records with an abstract as denominator; each pattern is a case-insensitive Python regular expression over title plus abstract, named in backticks and listed exactly in "Exact keyword patterns" (AI-Research Notes). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. Counts are lower bounds; the window is the journal's whole life, not five years. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | `experiment` 120 of 352 (34.1%); `between_subjects` 41 (11.6%); `questionnaire_survey_study` 68 (19.3%); `prereg_osf` 19 (5.4%, counts any mention, including "non-preregistered") |
| Qualitative interviews | 3 | `interview` 25 of 352 (7.1%); `qualitative_study` 13 (3.7%). Reading the first 8 `interview` matches: 5 clearly report interviews or thematic analysis of participant responses (for example https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbah.2025.100144 and https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbah.2023.100002), 2 apply thematic analysis to reviewed literature (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbah.2023.100022, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbah.2026.100323) and 1 is unclear from the excerpt (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbah.2025.100219) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | `autoethnography` zero of 352. A single-author phenomenological account with a first-person narrator appears at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbah.2026.100258 |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | `conceptual_theoretical` 24 of 352 (6.8%); many matches are "conceptual framework" inside empirical or review papers, for example https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbah.2024.100062, so the share overstates purely conceptual papers. `philosophical` matches 4 (1.1%) |
| Mixed methods | 2 | `mixed_methods` 9 of 352 (2.6%) |
| Meta-analysis | 2 | `meta_analysis` 4 of 352 (1.1%); `systematic_review` (systematic or scoping review or meta-analysis) 20 (5.7%) |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Stated by the journal's guide: human-subject work must carry a statement of approval by the appropriate institutional committee, including the date and reference number, and a statement that informed consent was obtained; the guide cites the Declaration of Helsinki and asks for representative human populations (archived guide, copy dated 2024-06-03, https://web.archive.org/web/20240603021435/https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/computers-in-human-behavior-artificial-humans/publish/guide-for-authors) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author articles are 52 of 350 (14.9%) in OpenAlex for 2023-01-01 to 2026-11-23, and 53 of 355 (14.9%) in Crossref author lists |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The archived guide asks for the affiliation where the work was done and states no rule on unaffiliated authors; no count of unaffiliated authors was made |
| **Data transparency requirement** | The archived guide says the journal "encourages and enables" sharing of supporting data where appropriate, with data linking and citation in the reference list; sharing is encouraged, not required |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double anonymized review (archived guide; DOAJ), so author identity is withheld from reviewers; preprints are allowed anywhere at any time (archived guide), and a public preprint may reveal identity |
| **AI use** | Disclosure statement before the reference list; AI may not be an author (archived guide, 2024-06-03) |
| **Open access and cost** | Gold open access; discounted APC USD 810 for articles submitted by 2026-12-31, full APC USD 1,620 (journal home copy, 2025-08-25); DOAJ records a waiver policy (https://doaj.org/api/search/journals/issn:2949-8821) |
| **Originality screening** | Submissions may be checked with Crossref Similarity Check (archived guide) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the journal's aims text states it examines artificial agents and human interaction with them from a psychological perspective and focuses on psychological or societal aspects, not purely technical issues (Framing Requirements; journal home copy, 2025-08-25). A purely technical AI paper is outside the stated scope.
- **Ethics statements**: human-subject work needs an approval statement with date and reference number and an informed-consent statement (Practical Concerns, IRB; archived guide, 2024-06-03).
- **AI use**: undisclosed generative AI use in writing breaches the stated policy (AI Policy).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; word limits and article types are unknown (Format blanks), and the guide copy is from 2024.

### Soft Tax

- **Cost**: gold open access, with an APC of USD 810 after a discount valid for submissions until 2026-12-31 and USD 1,620 without it (Open Access; home copy, 2025-08-25). The discount has been renewed at least once (free in 2024, discounted in 2025), but no page says it will continue after 2026.
- **Anonymisation**: review is double anonymized, so the manuscript must conceal author identity, and a public preprint may reveal it (Peer Review, Practical Concerns).
- **Time**: the publisher displays 57 days to first decision and 129 days to acceptance (Review Cycle Time; displayed figures, definitions not given).

### Best Suited For

- Experimental and questionnaire studies of people interacting with AI, robots and chatbots: `experiment` 34.1%, `user_study_participants` 38.1%, `human_ai_interaction` 21.9% of 352 abstracts (Methodological Preferences, Orientation).
- Qualitative and interview-based work on AI use: `interview` 7.1% of abstracts, and a qualitative study of ChatGPT adopters is among the most cited items (Methodological Preferences, Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Work on ethics, mental health, education and healthcare uses of AI: `ethics` 13.6%, `mental_health` 16.2%, `education_students` 21.9%, `healthcare` 17.0% (Sensitive Topics, Orientation).
- Authors who want open access with a licence choice: CC BY, CC BY-NC or CC BY-NC-ND per DOAJ (Preprint Policy).

### Not Recommended For

- Formal, algorithmic or proof-based AI work: `theorem_proof_complexity` matches 3 of 352 abstracts and `reinforcement_learning` 1 (Orientation; the aims text excludes purely technical issues). This shows rarity, not rejection.
- Authors needing a stated word limit or article-type guidance before choosing: none is readable (Format blanks).
- Authors who need a verified turnaround: the only figures are publisher displays without definitions, and the "review time" and "submission to acceptance" figures do not nest (Review Cycle Time).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours that exist in this corpus, listed only because they share the subject area; they are not a claim about acceptance odds.

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Computers in Human Behavior](computers-in-human-behavior.md) | Same publisher family; the aims text calls this journal complementary to it. An entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 2 | [International Journal of Social Robotics](international-journal-of-social-robotics.md) | Shares the social-robot subject (`social_robot` 15.9% of abstracts); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
| 3 | [ACM Transactions on Human-Robot Interaction](acm-transactions-on-human-robot-interaction.md) | Shares the human-robot interaction subject (top OpenAlex topic "Social Robot Interaction and HRI", 199 assignments); an entry exists in this corpus. No fit evidence collected here |
